Compak® Sporting: the compact format

A full Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ course needs a lot of land: woods, hills and several layouts. Many clubs do not have that. So the idea came up to bring the variety of sporting targets onto a small plot.

Compak® Sporting This is how Compak® Sporting began. Its rules state that the discipline was created in 1989 and adopted by FITASC in 1991, so it is a format of the late 20th century. It spread quickly: FITASC has held European Championships since 1995 and World Championships since 2004.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 1 · What Compak® Sporting is

Compak® Sporting The idea is one field. A Compak field has 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line. The targets fly over a marked rectangle in front of the shooters. They go in many directions, as in Sporting™, but all on one field.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 2 · Six traps, A to F

The format has several advantages. A club needs less land and fewer traps. Shooting moves faster. And spectators can see the whole squad (the group of shooters who shoot a round together) and all the targets from one spot, so Compak® Sporting works well on video.

Compak® Sporting The name and the rules of Compak® Sporting are a trade mark registered and protected by FITASC. That is why we write the ® sign and do not invent other versions of the name.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 1 · What Compak® Sporting is

Today Compak® Sporting is often a beginner's first discipline. It is easier to find near home, and its skills carry over to a full Sporting™ course. How a Compak field works in detail: How a Compak® Sporting layout works.

Key points

  • Compak® Sporting is a compact form of sporting on one field.
  • The rules say it was created in 1989 and adopted by FITASC in 1991.
  • One field: 6 traps lettered A to F and 5 shooting stations in a line.
  • The name and the rules are a trade mark of FITASC.

Did you know?

In Compak® Sporting a spectator can stay in one place and see all the targets of a round. On a full Sporting™ course that is not possible.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Why was Compak® Sporting created?

    1. To fit varied targets onto a small plot
    2. To bring back live-bird shooting
    3. To replace the Olympic clay events
    Answer

    To fit varied targets onto a small plot

    Compak® Sporting needs less land but keeps varied trajectories.

  2. How many stations and traps does a Compak® Sporting field have?

    1. 1 station and 15 traps
    2. 5 stations and 6 traps
    3. 8 stations and 2 traps
    Answer

    5 stations and 6 traps

    Five stations stand in a line, and six traps, A to F, throw the targets.

  3. When did FITASC adopt Compak® Sporting?

    1. In 1960
    2. In 1921
    3. In 1991
    Answer

    In 1991

    The discipline was created in 1989 and adopted by FITASC in 1991.
